title: Conditional Probability
notes: **Probability definition:** P(E) = n(E)/n(S) for classical probability, where n(E) = favorable outcomes, n(S) = total outcomes.
**Axiomatic definition:** P(E)≥0, P(S)=1, P(A∪B) = P(A)+P(B) for disjoint events.
**Independent events:** A and B are independent if P(A∩B) = P(A)·P(B).
**Fact.** P(E) = favourable/total. Additive law: P(A∪B) = P(A)+P(B)−P(A∩B). If mutually exclusive, P(A∪B)=P(A)+P(B).
**Fact.** Multiplicative: P(A∩B) = P(A)P(B|A); independence: P(A∩B) = P(A)P(B).
**Fact.** Complement: P(A') = 1 − P(A). For discrete: ΣP = 1; expected value E(X) = Σxᵢpᵢ.
